title: The Broadacres Rag (Traumatic Character Limit Mix)

lines.text: [Intro — Ragtime Guitar, Upright Bass, Brushes]
Well, Momma’s hollerin’, “Get your ass outta bed!”
Rooster’s been up since half-past dead
[Verse 1]
Down on Broadacres Road where the farmland lay flat
Horses in the pasture and a half-wild cat
Eleven acres, brick house built in nineteen-oh
Concrete basement said twenty-nine down below
Barn out back and a corrugated shop
Walnuts by the bushel and apples by the crop
Cherry trees, plum trees, firs out front
And Dad had broken cars parked wherever he’d want
Two old Citroëns and a Dasher gone wrong
Scott rolled that bastard before too long
Slalomed yellow lines at eighty for fun
Which is how farm boys learn what should not be done
[Chorus]
It was the Broadacres Rag
Mud on your boots and hay in the bag
Smelled like manure when summer came
Then hops rolled in and changed the game
We had chores at dawn and hell by noon
BB guns underneath the moon
We didn’t know paradise looked like that
We were too damn busy with the Broadacres Rag
[Verse 2]
Gregorys next door were cowboy stock
Rusty and Lynn and the whole damn flock
Shawn, Justin, David, rope and ride
Could wrestle a bull and come out upright
Grampa Chuck and Margaret too
Like family even when blood wasn’t true
Across the road the Kotnikov clan
Nice folks mostly till the mothers began
Calling the cops over boys being boys
Pushing and shoving and making noise
Half the time nobody knew who swung first
But everybody knew whose mother was worse
[Verse 3]
Then there were the Meuslings, machine-shop crew
Jehovah’s Witnesses and drift boats too
Paul talked different but he thought real fast
Bright as hell and built to last
The Wolfes had Billy, Buddy and Missy in tow
If trouble had children, you already know
Buddy stole my XR80 and tack from the barn
Which put a little dent in neighborhood charm
Will ran with Buddy and partied too young
A little too much before life had begun
But mostly we never locked truck or door
Left keys in the tractor like nobody stole anymore
[Chorus]
It was the Broadacres Rag
Mud on your boots and hay in the bag
Smelled like manure when summer came
Then hops rolled in and changed the game
We had chores at dawn and hell by noon
BB guns underneath the moon
We didn’t know paradise looked like that
We were too damn busy with the Broadacres Rag
[Verse 4]
Jess Owre owned half the ground in sight
Dennis helped keep the whole thing tight
Big fields stretching nearly forever
Farm crews working through any weather
Local boys and crews from Mexico way
Oaxaca voices in the heat of day
Different homes, same dust in the lung
Same sun overhead when the harvest was young
Nacho Palacios was my first best friend
Ignacio, I learned, when we got older again
Funny how a name can grow with the years
Same kid, same grin, just different ears
[Instrumental Turn — Ragtime Guitar and Harmonica]
[Verse 5]
We had a treehouse hid behind Douglas fir
Where good ideas went to die in a blur
We threw brown pinecones at cars passing by
Then Billy grabbed green ones and let ’em fly
THUMP on a Ford and the brakes locked down
Backup lights shining like judgment had found
Some redneck climbed out with murder in mind
And six farm boys disappeared behind
Invisible rifles became plywood guns
Army all afternoon under Oregon sun
Touch football, tag, hide-and-seek
Broken basketball hoop at the Wolfes every week
Possums got hunted, mailboxes learned fear
Horse apples flew when somebody got near
We TP’d yards and hayed ’em for flair
And somehow survived the shit we did there
[Chorus — Bigger]
It was the Broadacres Rag
Mud on your boots and hay in the bag
Smelled like manure when summer came
Then hops rolled in and changed the game
We had chores at dawn and hell by noon
BB guns underneath the moon
We didn’t know paradise looked like that
We were too damn busy with the Broadacres Rag
[Verse 6]
Scott and me rode pigs, or gave it a try
Went wallowing with ’em till clean skin said goodbye
Mom hosed us down by the back porch rail
Like two muddy convicts fresh outta jail
Goats and chickens and horses and dogs
Rabbit pellets, nettles and half-rotten logs
Poison oak taught lessons nobody forgot
And every strange turd got inspected on the spot
Fretsee the cat would vanish for days
Then weeks, then months in mysterious ways
Till one day she wandered off out of sight
And never came home from whatever cat night
[Bridge — Pull Back, Softer]
Summer tasted like lemonade
Sun tea sweating in the shade
Apple pie when Grandma came
Strawberry rhubarb did the same
Grandpa Norby watched the game
Hamm’s or Rainier, always the same
Chesterfield Kings and walnuts cracked
One by one with the seasons stacked
The tavern stood where the old road bent
Store, fuel pump, local government
They said upstairs had girls for hire
Before a hundred years and one good fire
[Verse 7 — Reflective]
There were Bible camps and family days
Holidays glowing in ordinary ways
Not much snow, but somehow bright
Like childhood made its ow
